summary: Router 0.23.1 / agent 0.31.0, ADR-0073. (1) render-env.sh and render-monitoring.sh source their secret-store access only from /etc/skirnir-router-secrets/render-env.conf (overridable for tests only via RENDER_ENV_* environment variables, which the units do not set); before sourcing it or SECRET_STORE_AUTH_FILE they resolve the path with readlink -f and refuse (render nothing, exit 0) when it lies under /etc/skirnir-router, /var/lib/skirnir-router or /var/log/skirnir-router, when the file or its folder is not owned by uid 0, or is group/other writable; the old location is never read. deploy.py pushes the access file to the new folder (install -d -m 0700) and removes the old copy; install.sh creates the folder and moves an existing old file. The router unit adds ReadOnlyPaths=-/etc/skirnir-router/certs and InaccessiblePaths=-/etc/skirnir-router-secrets; the secrets, refresh and cert helper units add NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, kernel protections, RestrictSUIDSGID, LockPersonality and UMask where it does not affect their job. (2) Agent tunnel: requests without a configured route reach the upstream only for an exact allow-list of inference, listing and version paths with their methods; anything else gets 403 path_not_allowed_on_node and a log line, without an upstream call. The existing route test changed accordingly (/rerank without a route is refused instead of forwarded). (3) Ollama update orders older than the installed version (live /api/version, else the binary's version) or not a plain release are refused before any download unless ollama_update.allow_downgrade is set; an unknown installed version keeps the previous behaviour.

findings.evidence: The router runs as uid 0 without capabilities with /etc/skirnir-router writable; owner bits let it rewrite the root-owned render-env.conf, which the daily secrets timer sources with full root; the same applied to render-monitoring.sh.
findings.resolution: The access file moves to a root-only folder the router unit cannot see; both renderers refuse files in router-writable paths or with loose ownership/modes before sourcing.

findings.evidence: Tunnel.handle forwarded every path without a configured route to Ollama, including /api/pull, /api/create, /api/delete and /api/blobs, on nodes where Ollama runs as LocalSystem.
findings.resolution: Exact allow-list in the agent; CI checks it covers every path the router sends and none it forbids.

findings.evidence: The router chose any Ollama version for an update order; only the archive checksum was verified.
findings.resolution: Downgrade and pre-release refusal unless ollama_update.allow_downgrade, like the agent's own update.

tests.evidence: all passed; a mutation that removed the auth-file check made it fail (1 failure).
ok; TestPassthroughOnlyInferencePaths, TestPassthroughAllowsNoModelManagement, TestOllamaDowngradeRefused, TestTunnelRoutes ran.

tests.command: all python test/... commands of ci.yml and security.yml (WSL); check_pinned_references, selftest_pinned_references, check_control_flow, check_adr_index, selftest_english_names (Windows)
tests.evidence: No failures except the two git-based checks under WSL (worktree path), which pass on Windows; ADR index ok: 73 ADRs.

limitations: The unit directives were not started under systemd here; the rollout verifies them on the router host (secrets service run, write probe in the router's mount namespace).
The router still runs as root; a dedicated user, the Linux agent unit and a LocalSystem child from a user-writable path remain open under TM-14.
Merged main after the PRs below it.
